Quick Start

This path produces a working first terminal in a few minutes.

Fastest option: open the Français — Modèles or English — Templates folder in this Compendium, import a Journal into the world, then rename it and assign a unique terminal ID before publishing it.

  1. Create a Foundry Journal.
  2. Add a page of the Terminal type and name it Main Menu.
  3. Give it the page ID main.
  4. Write a heading, a short message, and an automatic menu in its source.
  5. From the Journal header, open Configure Terminal, choose this page as Home, and enable Published.
  6. Grant the group Observer ownership on the Journal.
  7. Open the Terminals Scene Control and test with a player account.

Every module action lives in the Journal header menu, behind the ⋮ button.

# CENTRAL TERMINAL

System online.

::menu children
::end

The Terminals Scene Control opens the launcher your players will use.

Important: publication makes a terminal discoverable in the launcher, while Foundry permissions determine who can actually read it.

Create and Configure a Terminal

The root Journal

A terminal is a Journal containing one or more Terminal pages. Keep pages belonging to the same fictional device in one Journal.

Identity

  • Enabled: allows the terminal to be used.
  • Terminal ID: a short, stable, unique identifier such as security-console.
  • Label: the name presented to players.
  • Home page: the page opened at launch and with the Home key.
  • Theme: the terminal’s general appearance.

Behavior

  • Remember page: each user resumes their last page in individual mode.
  • Boot sequence: plays the CRT animation when opened.
  • Close with Escape at root: closes the terminal when history is empty.

One window, four tabs

Configuration, page structure, theme, and synchronized presentation share a single window. Changes are saved as soon as a field loses focus, so there is no Save button.

The Terminal ID is generated from the label and stays read-only until you click the pencil, so a macro or link that already points at it cannot break by accident.

Use the Open button at the bottom to test the terminal before play.

Write Pages and Menus

IDs and hierarchy

Every page needs a unique lowercase Page ID without spaces. The Parent field contains the ID of the page that should list it as a child. Menu label and sort order control its presentation.

The Parent field is a dropdown listing the other pages of the Journal, so an ID can never be mistyped.

Automatic menu

Lists the visible children of the current page:

::menu children
::end

Explicit menu

A local link targets a page ID. A UUID link can target a page in another Journal.

::menu
[PERSONNEL](terminal:personnel)
[ARCHIVES](@UUID[JournalEntry.abc.JournalEntryPage.def])
@UUID[JournalEntry.abc.JournalEntryPage.def]
@UUID[JournalEntry.abc.JournalEntryPage.def]{ARCHIVES}
::end

A bare UUID takes the target document's own name as its label. Foundry's {Label} suffix overrides it.

Other directives

  • ::login creates a code input leading to a success page.
  • ::image displays an image stored in the world or module.
  • ::effect glitch presents a block with a visual effect.

Headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, links, and inline code are supported. Arbitrary HTML and JavaScript are not.

Drop a Journal or a page onto the editor to insert a link to it.

Complete Example: Orpheus Security Console

Scene objective: the players inspect personnel files, discover a password, open the archives, and then the GM reveals a secret report at the right moment.

Journal structure

NameIDParentInitial state
Main Menumain—Visible, available
Personnel FilespersonnelmainVisible, available
Secure ArchivesarchivesmainVisible, password locked
Incident 1979incident-1979archivesHidden, available

1. Main Menu

Page type: Menu.

# SECURITY CONSOLE — ORPHEUS STATION

Connection established. Select a file.

::menu children
::end

2. Personnel Files

Menu label: PERSONNEL FILES.

# PERSONNEL FILES

- Commander: Lena Voss
- Engineer: Marc Tannhäuser
- Physician: Dr Elise Ward

Internal note: temporary Omega code ORPHEUS-79.

3. Secure Archives

Choose Visible + locked, lock type Password, secret ORPHEUS-79, and failure message ACCESS DENIED — OMEGA CLEARANCE REQUIRED.

# SECURE ARCHIVES

Omega authorization confirmed.

::menu children
::end

4. Incident 1979

Prepare this page as Hidden + available.

# INCIDENT 1979

The signal did not originate outside the station.

The transmitter was already inside Laboratory B.

Running the scene

  1. Players see Personnel and Archives; Archives is marked as locked.
  2. The personnel file gives them the password ORPHEUS-79.
  3. After unlocking, Archives opens, but its child menu is empty.
  4. At the dramatic moment, the GM opens Terminal Structure and reveals incident-1979.
  5. Without editing Archives, INCIDENT 1979 automatically appears the next time its menu is displayed.

The same example works in synchronized presentation: the GM selects one controller and the whole group watches their progress without intermediate approval.

Reveal, Hide, and Lock

Visibility and access are independent mechanisms.

StateResult
HiddenThe page is omitted from automatic menus and cannot be opened by players.
Visible + availableThe page appears and opens normally.
Visible + lockedThe page appears with a lock and asks for its access method.

Lock types

  • None: appropriate when access is available.
  • GM only: only a GM can pass the lock.
  • Password: the player must enter the configured value.

The Structure tab of the terminal configuration lets you prepare every page before play, then reveal, hide, lock, or unlock it quickly during the session. Automatic menus are recalculated whenever displayed.

Avoid placing secrets in the name of a Journal or visible page: a lock protects access, but not necessarily every label exposed by Foundry.

Permissions and Publication

Two complementary controls

  1. In Foundry Journal permissions, grant Observer to users who should read the terminal.
  2. In Configure Terminal, enable Published to add it to the player launcher.

Publication never bypasses permissions. Conversely, a readable but unpublished Journal can still be opened by UUID or by the GM, but does not appear in the launcher.

Before play

  • Check permissions on the root Journal and every page linked from another Journal.
  • Test with an actual player account: GM debug mode can expose normally hidden pages.
  • Use publication sort order to organize multiple terminals.
  • Only make pages public when they should be immediately discoverable.

The Terminals Scene Control opens the launcher. A player only sees published terminals they are permitted to observe.

Synchronized Presentation

This mode makes the group feel as though everyone is watching the same screen.

  1. Open the terminal or its Journal.
  2. Choose Manage synchronization.
  3. Select one connected user as controller.
  4. Start the session.

The controller then navigates freely. The GM does not approve each action. Every other user sees the same page, selected menu row, Back/Home history, and session unlocks. Their controls are disabled.

Transfer control

The GM can reopen management and select another user at any time. If the controller disconnects, the session remains frozen until control is transferred. Reconnecting restores the latest known state.

Requirements

  • Only one synchronized session can be active in the world.
  • Every user must be permitted to view the displayed page.
  • Navigation to a page hidden from or forbidden to an observer is safely rejected.

Themes and Effects

Appearance resolves from the broadest level to the most specific:

  1. world default theme;
  2. theme selected in terminal configuration;
  3. optional page override;
  4. terminal customizations.

The Theme Editor adjusts colors, brightness, contrast, typography, scanlines, vignette, noise, and glitch. Maintain sufficient reading contrast and test on the display used during play.

The preview at the top of the tab repaints as you drag a control, so a look can be dialled in without opening the terminal.

The client-side Screen effects setting disables CRT animations and effects for a user who needs it. It changes neither content nor the theme selected for anyone else.

Use page overrides sparingly. They work well to signal a different system, an alarm, or a remote connection, but too much variation weakens a terminal’s identity.

Operate During Play

Keyboard controls

  • Up/Down: move the selection.
  • Enter: activate the selected element.
  • 1 through 9: select a menu entry directly.
  • Escape: return to the previous page.
  • Home: return to the home page.

The mouse remains available. During synchronized presentation, only the controller can activate commands.

During the session

  • Keep the Structure window open to change prepared states quickly.
  • Reveal a page before players try to open it if it should appear in an automatic menu.
  • Session unlocks are temporary to that terminal session; they do not change the page’s editorial state.
  • UUID links can cross into another Journal, but its permissions always apply.

Pre-session Checklist

  • ☐ The Journal has a valid home page.
  • ☐ Every page ID is unique and parent fields use those IDs.
  • ☐ Menus and UUID links have been previewed.
  • ☐ Secret pages are hidden or locked for the intended effect.
  • ☐ No secret appears in a visible label.
  • ☐ The Journal and linked Journals grant the correct Observer permissions.
  • ☐ The terminal is enabled and published if players should find it themselves.
  • ☐ The theme remains readable with effects enabled and disabled.
  • ☐ Testing was performed with a player account.
  • ☐ For synchronized presentation, the intended controller is connected.

A robust workflow is to create all content ahead of time, leave it hidden, then use the Structure window to orchestrate its discovery.

Troubleshooting

The terminal does not appear in the launcher

Confirm it is enabled and published, has a home page, and the player has Observer permission on the Journal.

A page is missing from an automatic menu

Check its ID, Parent field, parent-menu option, visibility, and Foundry permissions.

“File unavailable”

The target is missing, hidden, forbidden to the user, or its UUID is stale. Open the Structure window and correct reported diagnostics.

Synchronization refuses to start or navigate

At least one world user cannot see the Journal or target page. Align permissions before trying again.

Code changes do not appear loaded

Reload the world after changing the manifest or Compendium. During development, rebuild the pack with npm run build:packs. For a release, the workflow automatically rebuilds both the Compendium and minified bundle.
